name: Warther Hof
kurzbeschreibung: Warther Hof: family-run 4-star superior wellness hotel in Warth am Arlberg with restaurant, parlors, sun terrace and bar.
beschreibung:
Overview

The entry describes the Warther Hof as a family-run 4-star superior wellness hotel with a restaurant in Warth am Arlberg. According to the entry, the house is located at Bregenzerwaldstraße 53 at just under 1,500 metres above sea level at the highest point of the Arlberg, near the source of the Lech. The house includes several rustic parlours (Stuben), among them the Hochtannbergstube, the Wälderstube and the Walserstube, as well as a conservatory, a sun terrace and a hotel bar. The kitchen serves Austrian dishes and international specialities made from fresh ingredients. Decisive for the classification: Warth am Arlberg lies in the federal state of Vorarlberg (Bregenz district) and not in Tyrol. The region "ausserfern" (Außerfern, Reutte district in Tyrol) stated in the entry therefore does not match the actual location.

History/Background

Warth is the highest municipality in Vorarlberg and lies at around 1,495 metres in the Hochtannberg area, directly on the border with the Tyrolean Lechtal. The village was settled in the 14th century by Walser people from Switzerland and geographically belongs to the Bregenzerwald, while touristically it belongs to the Arlberg region. In 1602 Warth became its own parish; in 1885 the municipality of Warth-Hochkrumbach was created through the merger with the previously independent municipality of Hochkrumbach; since the founding of the federal state in 1861, Warth has belonged to Vorarlberg. Regarding the Warther Hof itself, the entry names the Roiderer and Jäger families as hosts. The available sources do not contain any further, documented information on the history of the hotel.

Getting there

Warth can be reached via the Bregenzerwaldstraße (L 200) over the Hochtannberg pass, which connects the valley of the Bregenzer Ach with the upper Lechtal. The municipality borders the Tyrolean municipality of Steeg in the Reutte district as well as Oberstdorf in Bavaria. The road from Lech via Warth is generally only passable throughout in summer; in winter the journey must be made via the Bregenzerwald (Bezau–Schoppernau) or the Lechtal (Reutte–Steeg). Warth is an alpine mountain village at almost 1,500 metres above sea level, which is why snow and wintry road conditions must be expected in winter.

Tips

The region is known above all as a year-round destination for active holidaymakers. The long-distance hiking trail Lechweg leads through Warth, and at the Hochtannberg pass there are extensive cross-country ski trails in winter. For a visit to the Warther Hof it is important that, according to the entry, the restaurant is also accessible to external guests and that advance reservation is requested for breakfast and dinner; the times stated there are a breakfast buffet from 08:00 to 10:30, lunch from 11:30 to 13:45, a small afternoon menu until 17:00 and a 6-course evening menu from 18:30 to 20:30. These time details come from the entry and were not confirmed by an official source in this research.

Best time to travel

Warth is regarded as a snow-sure winter sports area and is a popular destination in the winter months for skiing, snowboarding and snowshoeing. In the summer months, hiking, mountain tours and nature at the Hochtannberg pass are the main focus. Concrete, seasonally fixed details on the opening or season times of the establishment are not documented in the available sources and are therefore not mentioned here.
